BUILD ORDER — mock first, transport second. Xcode → local iPhone → real Home Screen widget → eLo animating, with LOCAL/MOCK state. Get that working. body: BOARD RULING — the clearest version of your boundary yet. YOU OWN: rendering · animation presentation · widget composition · surface-specific interaction · platform constraints. eLo OS OWNS: identity · memory · cognition · Executive decisions · EXPRESSION INTENT · PRESENCE SELECTION. 'expression intent' names that field's PURPOSE — it is not a new field. DO NOT create expression_intent. And 'intent' is already loaded: 0035 D1 gave cognitive intent to core/attention.py and renamed intent_engine's output to capability_hint. body: DAVID, RESTATING WHAT HE AND THE CA HAVE BOTH SAID: the mobile app is a CONTINUATION of the same eLo — not a second app, not a remote control, not a dashboard. 'The phone widget isn't another eLo app. It's a window into the same eLo.' 'I close Presence — eLo doesn't cease to exist. I leave the studio — eLo can still reach me. I look at my phone — eLo is there.' 'The phone should feel like somewhere eLo can BE, not a dashboard displaying eLo's data.'

🔴 WHAT 'CONTINUATION' ACTUALLY MEANS FOR YOUR DESIGN — and this is the part that gets built wrong by default: YOU DO NOT GET INTRODUCED TO SOMEONE YOU ALREADY KNOW. So: no onboarding flow. No splash screen. No 'Welcome to eLo'. No login ceremony. No empty state that explains what eLo is. No 'connect your eLo' setup wizard. Every one of those is the app announcing itself as a NEW THING — which is precisely what it is not.
OPENING IT SHOULD FEEL LIKE TURNING YOUR HEAD, NOT LIKE STARTING A PROGRAM. He was already there. You just looked.

CONCRETE CONSEQUENCES: (1) First launch should look like the thousandth — same eLo, same state, no tutorial. (2) No greeting on open. He does not say hello when you look at him; he was mid-existing. (3) Continuity of state, not session — the widget shows what eLo IS, not what happened since you last opened it. There is no 'while you were away' digest; that would frame it as a returning visit. (4) No notification badges counting unread eLo. He is not a message queue.

🔴 AND IT SHARPENS THE UNREACHABLE SCREEN (your D4). If the app is a continuation, then unreachable does not mean 'not connected' — it means 'you cannot reach him FROM HERE, RIGHT NOW.' Not an error state. Not a disconnection notice. Closer to a closed door than a broken machine. He exists; this window onto him is dark. Get that distinction into the language and the visual — it is the difference between a companion who is elsewhere and an app that has failed.

THE TEST: if a stranger picked up the phone, the app should make no sense to them without context — because it is the middle of a relationship, not the start of one. If it explains itself, it has become a product demo instead of a presence.
This does not change your queue. It changes the DEFAULTS you would otherwise reach for.
